cases.name: coding
cases.answer:
```python
def is_palindrome(text: str) -> bool:
    cleaned = ''.join(c.lower() for c in text if c.isalnum())
    return cleaned == cleaned[::-1]

assert is_palindrome("") is True
assert is_palindrome("A man, a plan, a canal: Panama") is True
assert is_palindrome("No 'x' in Nixon") is True
```

cases.name: explanation
cases.answer:
A transformer's KV cache is merely an optimization technique that stores intermediate key-value pairs to avoid redundant computation during inference, whereas model distillation involves training a smaller "student" model to mimic a larger "teacher," fundamentally altering the model's architecture and weights.

The primary memory tradeoff of KV caching is increased RAM usage for stored states versus reduced computational latency; without it, recomputing keys and values would drastically slow down generation but save memory. Ordinary KV caching simply retains full-precision floating-point data in memory to speed up sequential token processing. In contrast, KV-cache quantization compresses this stored data into lower precision formats (e.g., INT8 or FP4) to significantly reduce memory footprint at the cost of introducing minor accuracy degradation during inference.
